page0.text:
The mountain is rumbling.
Dark clouds shroud the sky, and the trees seem to tremble nervously due to the tremors.
...
Saber watches it all from the mountain gate.
She sensed it as soon as she felt the noxious, indescribable aura oozing from Ryudou Temple.
The golden Servant isn't the only one awaiting her at the top of these stairs.
Something aberrant lies in wait for her and her allies.

page1.text:
"..."
She can't make any mistakes up ahead.
If the summit is going to be the place where they die, then she will be the one to face the threat of death.
She hopes the other two can survive this ominous realm.

page2.text:
For their sakes, she can't afford to hold back.
She can fire her sacred sword twice.
She's well aware that she will disappear the instant she uses it the second time.

page3.text:
"No matter. This was never an opponent we could beat unscathed."
Gilgamesh, the King of Heroes.
The only way to defeat the man with a thousand Noble Phantasms is with a decisive strike from her sacred sword.
"See you, Saber. Start after thirty minutes."
She recalls Rin's words.
There is one minute left until the appointed time.
Saber breathes in deeply and considers her condition.

page4.text:
A breeze blows from the summit.
She begins up the stone steps once the ill wind begins to shake the trees.

page5.text:
She dashes up the steps in a single breath.
As soon as she stepped foot on the stairs, the enemy would have realized her assault.
The last Servant she needs to defeat should appear within the temple grounds.
She needs to get there as fast as she can and defeat Gilgamesh before Rin and Shirou arrive.

page6.text:
...She isn't defying her Master's orders.
She began her assault after thirty minutes, just as Rin commanded.
Even if she enters the temple grounds earlier than expected and engages Gilgamesh, that isn't a violation of her orders.
She's just deviated from her Master's projections in the course of protecting her Master's life.

page7.text:
...
While the air from the summit is putrid, she is like a gust of cleansing wind that cuts at the rot as she ascends the steps.
It will take her less than a minute to reach the temple.
That should put her about five minutes ahead of Rin's projections.
It will give her plenty of time to end the battle with Gilgamesh.

page8.text:
"Ha!"
She runs, enduring the ominous chill from the mountain gate.
Like a silver speeding bullet, she races toward the summit.

page9.text:
Just as she comes up to the gate...
"What...?"
She didn't mean to stop, but she comes to a sudden halt.
Sweat coats her forehead.
Saber gazes up at the mountain gate in astonishment.

page10.text:
"I've been waiting. I'm glad you made it, Saber."
A smooth voice cuts through the night.
Moonlight glints off the 5-foot-long sword.
An enemy that shouldn't be here
stands at the top of the steps.

page11.text:
"Assassin..."
Her voice lacks its usual grace.
She's faced with an enemy, an obstacle, that shouldn't be here.
That fact robs her of her composure.

page12.text:
"What's wrong, Saber? Is it so strange to see me?
I am the gatekeeper here. You know that."
His voice is delighted, yet cool.
The swordsman seems completely unchanged, his back to the ill wind from the summit.

page13.text:
"This can't be. How are you here, Assassin!? Caster summoned you. You shouldn't be able to remain now that she's gone!"
"That would be true for a normal Servant. But I'm a special case. I'm bound not to a person, but to this land.
For me, this mountain gate is equivalent to the hosts you call Masters."

page14.text:
"The...land is your host?"
"Indeed. A Servant cannot maintain themselves without a physical body, even if one is a mage. Apparently, we need a host in the current era.
That vixen summoned me and chose this land as my host.
That's why I can only manifest at this mountain gate. I won't disappear as long as this gate exists, even if my summoner is gone."

page15.text:
"Still, I'm little more than a day laborer.
The vixen only gave me enough magical energy for twenty days. You can see for yourself how close I am to that limit."
The swordsman explains in a singsong voice and lifts his right arm.
In his elegant garment,
his pale arm is transparent like glass.

page16.text:
"Assassin, you..."
"As you can see, I won't even last until dawn.
I'm already past the twenty-day limit. I consider it a stroke of luck that I've lasted this long."

page17.text:
...
She looks up at the swordsman in shock.
His aura emits neither bloodlust nor hostility.
It simply demands combat.
He desires a pointless duel to the death, irrespective of victory or loss.

page18.text:
"So you stayed here to fight me, Assassin?"
"Don't make me spell it out, Saber. If I say it, that would be boring."

page19.text:
Assassin chuckles.
Saber can understand the swordsman's reasons.
But she doesn't have time for this.
Unless she hurries, her allies will arrive while she's fighting Gilgamesh.
No, in the worst case, they might arrive first and be forced to engage him without her.

page20.text:
"Move aside, Assassin. Caster ordered you to guard the gate, and she's gone. There's no point in guarding it now."
Saber takes a step forward.
However...
"No. For me, there is no point in fighting."
He declares that the duel will begin if she proceeds any further.
The tip of his long katana is pointed at Saber.

page21.text:
"Yes, there is no meaning to this duel. I've never had anything, after all. No pride as a Heroic Spirit, nor anything to wish for.
No... My summoning itself was a mistake. After all, I am not even Sasaki Kojirou."

page22.text:
"!?"
Saber is extremely confused.
Sasaki Kojirou.
That should be this Servant's True Name.
But Assassin has just admitted that he's an imposter.

page23.text:
"Don't be so surprised.
Sasaki Kojirou has always been a fictional swordsman with no identity.
He's believed to have existed, but the records about him are incredibly vague.
He is a fictional swordsman fabricated in histories to be a nemesis to a certain renowned swordmaster."

page24.text:
"A man named Sasaki Kojirou may well have existed. There was probably even a martial artist with a long sword named Monohoshizao.
But those traits don't belong to a single individual.
The swordsman Sasaki Kojirou was a fictional martial artist created as a character foil."

page25.text:
"You're a...fictional Heroic Spirit?"
"Yes. All I am is a swordsman who was deemed most suitable to wear the shell of Sasaki Kojirou.
I have no name. I don't even know how to read and write, and I wasn't wealthy enough to have a name of my own."

page26.text:
"I'm just a wraith summoned here for my ability to demonstrate the secret technique attributed to Sasaki Kojirou in the histories.
A fake Servant can't last long. That's why Caster treated me as expendable."

page27.text:
"See? There was never any point to my fights.
Even if I accomplished anything noteworthy, all the credit would go to 'Sasaki Kojirou.' I wouldn't profit from it at all. Everything is meaningless to me, because I am no one.
Even my own self isn't set in stone. I'm just a nameless, disposable swordsman who plays the role of Sasaki Kojirou."
The long sword sways.
The swordsman created as a fictional character stands in Saber's way, prepared to fulfill his role.

page28.text:
"But...
If there is any meaning to my existence, then it would be now.
If I, who died with no name, were to have a wish..."
Then surely, the nameless swordsman would have dreamed of facing a
superior swordsman, something he was never allowed to witness in life.

page29.text:
"Assassin."
She takes up her sword.
There is no persuading this foe.
The only response to a swordsman ready to lay down his life is to meet him with steel.

page30.text:
"Then, let us begin.
This body was always meant to die. There could be no greater ending to my life than to face you here!"
His long sword sweeps through the air.
Saber's sword parries the moonlit blade.

page31.text:
"Kh!"
The katana suddenly changes direction.
If she uses her strength against this man, she won't be strong enough to face Gilgamesh at the summit.
But she also can't afford to hold back against Assassin.
No—can she win even if she goes all out against him?

page32.text:
The katana's attacks grow sharper with each swing.
A fictional swordsman.
A master of the sword with no Noble Phantasm, who can fight on equal ground with Heroic Spirits.
She must settle this duel with him now.
